title: Four years, then a long afterlife: 34 moments
lede: From a New York incorporation to a trademark renewal in Los Angeles. Filter by thread.

events.title: Kozmo is founded
events.text: Inception date in the company’s financial statements. It is incorporated in New York and reincorporates in Delaware in August 1999.

events.title: First outside money
events.text: 1,133,332 Series A preferred shares are sold at $0.21 each.

events.title: First deliveries in New York
events.text: The first distribution center opens in New York City and the company begins recognizing revenue.

events.title: 3,700 customers, $155,000 of sales
events.text: The first year of operations ends with a net loss of $813,000. Series B shares are sold at $0.21.

events.title: Seattle
events.text: The second market opens.

events.title: San Francisco and Boston
events.text: Two more markets open in the same month.

events.title: Series D at $1.80
events.text: 15.6 million preferred shares are sold. Flatiron Partners and Oak Investment Partners join the board.

events.title: Washington, D.C.
events.text: The fifth market opens. Gerardo Burdo joins as chief financial officer and Kenneth Trevathan as chief operating officer.

events.title: Amazon invests
events.text: Series E shares are sold at $4.41. Amazon.com buys 13.6 million of them; its total investment is $60M.

events.title: $26.4M lost on $3.5M of sales
events.text: The year ends with 101,234 registered customers and $88.9M of cash.

events.title: Los Angeles
events.text: The sixth market opens.

events.title: The Starbucks agreement
events.text: Kozmo agrees to pay Starbucks $150M over five years for drop boxes and promotion in its stores. Starbucks has invested $25M in Kozmo.

events.title: Series F at $7.55
events.text: 15.3 million shares are issued, 4.0 million of them for agreements and stock, not cash. Kozmo signs a delivery agreement with Amazon.

events.title: IPO filing
events.text: Kozmo files to sell up to $150M of stock on the Nasdaq as KZMO. It has 2,665 employees (derived).

events.title: Chicago and Atlanta
events.text: Limited service begins in two more cities in the first week of April.

events.title: MSNBC report on delivery zones
events.text: MSNBC reports that Kozmo’s Washington delivery area leaves out nearly 350,000 of the city’s 400,000 black residents. Kozmo says it looks only at Internet usage. A lawsuit follows the same month.

events.title: More than 300 laid off
events.text: 275 couriers, dispatchers and field staff in New York and Los Angeles and 30 headquarters employees lose their jobs.

events.title: IPO withdrawn
events.text: Kozmo asks the SEC to withdraw the registration “because of unfavorable market conditions.” No shares were sold.

events.title: Lawsuit dismissed
events.text: The federal discrimination suit is dismissed at the plaintiffs’ request. Kozmo operates in 11 cities and widens its delivery areas in four of them.

events.title: No deal with Urbanfetch
events.text: Talks to buy the New York rival fall through. Days later Urbanfetch gives up consumer delivery.

events.title: Agreement with the Equal Rights Center
events.text: Kozmo commits $125,000 to Internet access programs in Washington. The announcement names Gerry Burdo as chief executive.

events.title: $30M promised
events.text: Investors promise $30M; E-Commerce Times names Flatiron Partners as the source. Kozmo says three markets were profitable in the month.

events.title: A delivery fee
events.text: Kozmo adds a charge of about $2 on orders below $25 to $30.

events.title: Houston and San Diego closed
events.text: 120 jobs are cut, about 6% of the workforce. Nine cities remain.

events.title: 60 more laid off
events.text: About half are in technology. Kozmo plans a 400,000-copy printed catalogue and says it will drop “.com” from its name on April 1.

events.title: Starbucks agreement abandoned
events.text: Kozmo says it will remove its 500 drop boxes from Starbucks stores.

events.title: PDQuick merger collapses
events.text: Talks with the Los Angeles online grocer end when PDQuick’s financing fails to arrive.

events.title: Kozmo shuts down
events.text: The company stops deliveries in all nine markets, lays off about 1,100 employees and says it will liquidate.

events.title: MaxDelivery
events.text: Former Kozmo technology chief Chris Siragusa is running a one-hour delivery service in lower Manhattan, with a $10 minimum.

events.title: A first claim on the name
events.text: EXIM Brands LLC of Evanston, Illinois applies to register KOZMO.COM. The application is abandoned in June 2008.

events.title: Yummy Foods registers KOZMO
events.text: Two registrations, for online grocery retail and for delivery, are issued to the Los Angeles company.

events.title: “Relaunching soon”
events.text: A placeholder page appears at kozmo.com.

events.title: Relaunch in Los Angeles
events.text: Yummy.com reopens Kozmo.com as an online warehouse club with a $35 minimum and a $5.99 delivery fee.

events.title: Registrations renewed
events.text: The USPTO records the renewal of both KOZMO registrations. The Internet Archive’s last capture of the site is dated May 20, 2022.
